title: Llegar a + Infinitive for Peaks and Limits

sections.content: You know *llegar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 25 for reaching a high point or extreme after a process. In reports on population and data, it highlights a peak, a record figure or a failure to recover despite time. Use it in the affirmative to mark a maximum point (*La tasa llegó a superar los diez puntos*) and in the negative to show that an expected level was never reached (*El repunte no llegó a consolidarse*). Notice that *llegar a* + infinitive expresses a threshold reached in a series, whereas *llegar a* + place means physical arrival.

sections.title: Peaks and unreached levels
rows: El descenso llegó a superar el diez por ciento.
ha llegado a + infinitive (up to now)
El envejecimiento ha llegado a duplicarse.
La natalidad no llegó a recuperarse.

items.spanish: En la última década, la tasa de envejecimiento llegó a duplicarse.
items.english: In the last decade, the ageing rate even doubled.

items.spanish: La natalidad mostró un ligero repunte, pero no llegó a superar el nivel anterior.
items.english: The birth rate showed a slight uptick, but did not manage to exceed the previous level.

items.spanish: El número de mayores de sesenta y cinco años ha llegado a alcanzar cifras históricas.
items.english: The number of people over sixty-five has reached historic figures.

sections.content: Do not drop the preposition *a* before the infinitive: *llegó a superar*, never *llegó superar*. And remember the contrast with *ir* + gerund: *fue descendiendo* follows the whole curve, while *llegó a descender* points to the extreme point the curve reached.
